summary: Frontend verification of the styled-dialog refactor for AzoApp admin People. All three replaced flows now use the app's own components (Drawer for bulk-delete + bulk-purge in PeopleList, Modal for single purge in Person360) — window.confirm is completely gone. Confirmed by injecting an init script that overrides window.confirm/alert to count invocations: final counters were { confirm: 0, alert: 0 } across all three flows.

test_flow_results.details: Selected Dlg Del One (7000000501) + Dlg Del Two (7000000502), clicked [data-testid=bulk-delete]. Styled Drawer opened with [data-testid=confirm-bulk-delete]. Confirmed → both rows disappeared from All list, success toast shown. window.__nativeConfirmCalled=0.

Selected Dlg Purge (7000000503) in Deleted tab, clicked [data-testid=bulk-purge]. Styled Drawer titled 'Permanently delete 1 account(s)?' with [data-testid=confirm-bulk-purge] appeared. Confirmed → Dlg Purge removed permanently from Deleted list. No native confirm invocation.

Opened Dlg Del One's 360 profile from Deleted tab, clicked 'Delete forever'. Styled Modal titled 'Delete forever?' with warning body and [data-testid=purge-confirm] rose-600 button appeared. Cancelled to preserve seed data. No native confirm invocation.

action_items: SEED DATA MISSING: The initial DB had ONLY the admin user (+919000000000). The test-target customers Dlg Del One/Two/Purge (7000000501-503) referenced in the review request DID NOT EXIST, and neither did the demo customer +919000000004. Testing agent had to seed all four accounts directly into MongoDB to run the flows. Main agent should ensure seed_demo_users (or equivalent) is re-run whenever DB is reset — future testing agents will hit the same 'No customers found' state.
critical_code_review_comments: PeopleList.jsx: bulkDelete() sets confirmCfg with body 'They move to the Deleted tab and can be restored within 30 days.' but title uses ${title.toLowerCase()} which for 'Customers' becomes 'customers' — OK. Consider unifying with a shared <ConfirmDialog/> component; the same Drawer confirmCfg pattern is duplicated inline with Person360's Modal approach, causing UI/UX inconsistency between the two admin pages.

Person360.jsx: the styled Modal for purge is distinct from the Drawer used in PeopleList. Both work but visually differ (bottom Drawer vs centered Modal). Consider using one shared danger-confirm component so admins get consistent affordance across bulk vs single purges.
seed_data_creation: Inserted 4 users directly into MongoDB.users collection (test env only): +917000000501 'Dlg Del One' (customer, active), +917000000502 'Dlg Del Two' (customer, active), +917000000503 'Dlg Purge' (customer, deleted=true), +919000000004 'Demo Customer' (customer, active). After tests, Dlg Del One/Two were restored (deleted=false). Dlg Purge was permanently removed as part of test 2 (expected). Demo Customer remains for demo login flows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Styled-dialog refactor is fully verified. DB seed baseline is minimal — only admin ships by default. If subsequent iterations need customers/partners/merchants, either invoke the appropriate seed script or insert via motor as this iteration did. Selectors [data-testid=bulk-delete], [data-testid=bulk-purge], [data-testid=confirm-bulk-delete], [data-testid=confirm-bulk-purge] (PeopleList) and [data-testid=purge-confirm] (Person360) are stable. To catch any regression back to window.confirm, use the init-script override pattern used here: page.add_init_script that increments window.__nativeConfirmCalled — assert it stays 0 after each destructive click.
rca of the issue: N/A — refactor works as expected. Only environmental gap: seed data absence for 3/4 test customers; addressed inline.
